books.section: Topic 1.4 Columbian Exchange, Spanish Exploration, and Conquest
The Early Colonial Era: Spain Colonizes the New World

options.text: Maize became a staple food on three continents, feeding population growth far beyond Mexico.
Maize replaced wheat as the main crop of Europe within a few years.
options.misconception: Maize added to European diets; it did not replace wheat in a few years.

options.text: Maize stayed a local crop of Mexico and never changed diets elsewhere.
options.misconception: Maize spread to Europe, Africa, and Asia after 1492; it did not stay local.

options.text: Maize spread only because European governments ordered farmers to plant it.
options.misconception: Farmers adopted maize because it grew well and fed more people, not because governments ordered it.

rationales.general:
1. Follow one seed around the world. Maize began in Mexico and spread across the Americas before 1492.
2. Watch it cross the ocean. After contact it reached Europe, then Africa and Asia.
3. Ask what changed. A hardy crop that fed more people supported population growth on three continents.
4. Rule out the rest. It did not stay local, replace wheat overnight, or spread by government order.
Remember: when a crop crosses oceans, ask how many mouths it fed.
rationales.A: Maize became a staple on three continents. A hardy crop that fed more people supported population growth far beyond Mexico.
rationales.B: Maize added to European diets. It did not replace wheat within a few years.
rationales.C: Maize spread to Europe, Africa, and Asia after 1492. It did not stay a local crop of Mexico.
rationales.D: Farmers adopted maize because it grew well and fed more people. No government ordered it planted.

stem: Maize first grew in Mexico, then spread across North America, and after 1492 it reached Europe, Africa, and Asia. Which statement best describes the historical significance of maize's spread?
